slides.title: Revision: Structure and Properties of Cell Membrane
slides.english_text:
Revision: Structure and Properties of Cell Membrane
• Cell membrane
• Phospholipid bilayer
• Functions
• Separate intracellular region and extracellular region
• Control substances entering and exiting the cell
• Property
• Selective permeability
• Cell membrane allows some substances to pass in different rates while it restricts certain other substances to pass

• Control substances entering and exiting the cell 控制物質進出細胞
• Property特性:
• Selective permeability 選擇性滲透性:

certain other substances to pass

slides.title: Passive Membrane Transport
slides.english_text:
Passive Membrane Transport
• Facilitated diffusion
• Certain polar water-soluble molecules (e.g. glucose, amino acids, and ions) are transported passively down their concentration gradient by:
• Carrier-mediated facilitated diffusion
• Substances bind to carrier proteins
• E.g. glucose, amino acids
• Channel-mediated facilitated diffusion
• Substances move through channel proteins
• E.g. calcium ions, sodium ions, potassium ions
slides.raw_bilingual_text:
Passive Membrane Transport
被動膜運輸

transported passively down their concentration gradient by:

沿其濃度梯度向下運輸：
• Carrier-mediated facilitated diffusion 載體介導的促進擴散
• Substances bind to carrier proteins 物質與載體蛋白結合
• E.g. glucose, amino acids 例如葡萄糖、胺基酸
• Channel-mediated facilitated diffusion 通道介導的促進擴散
• Substances move through channel proteins 物質通過通道蛋白移動
• E.g. calcium ions, sodium ions, potassium ions例如鈣離子、鈉離子、鉀離子

slides.title: • Tonicity
slides.english_text:
• Tonicity
• Ability of a solution to change the shape of cells by altering the cells’ internal water volume
• Isotonic solution has same tonicity as inside the cell, so volume of cell remains unchanged
• Hypertonic solution has higher osmolarity than inside cell, so water flows out of cell, resulting in cell shrinking
• Hypotonic solution has lower osmolarity than inside cell, so water flows into cell, resulting in cell swelling or bursting
slides.raw_bilingual_text:

remains unchanged

flows out of cell, resulting in cell shrinking

• Hypotonic solution has lower osmolarity than inside cell, so water
flows into cell, resulting in cell swelling or bursting

slides.title: Active Membrane Transport
slides.english_text:
Active Membrane Transport
• Two major types of active membrane transport methods
• Active transport
• Vesicular transport
• Both require cellular energy to move molecules across plasma membrane for any of these reasons:
• Molecule is too large for channel proteins
• Molecule is not lipid soluble
• Molecule is not able to move down concentration gradient
slides.raw_bilingual_text:
Active Membrane Transport
主動膜運輸
• Two major types of active membrane transport methods
兩種主要類型的主動膜運輸方法
• Active transport 主動運輸
• Vesicular transport 囊泡運輸/膜泡運輸
• Both require cellular energy to move molecules across plasma
membrane for any of these reasons:
兩者都需要細胞能量來移動分子穿過細胞膜，原因如下：
• Molecule is too large for channel proteins 分子對於通道蛋白來說太大
• Molecule is not lipid soluble 分子不溶於脂質
• Molecule is not able to move down concentration gradient
分子無法沿濃度梯度向下移動
13

slides.title: Active Membrane Transport
slides.english_text:
Active Membrane Transport
• Active Transport
• Requires special carrier proteins (pumps )
• Moves molecules against their concentration gradient (from low to high) ○ This requires energy directly or indirectly ○ Some pumps transport more than one substance
• Antiporters
• transport one substance into cell while transporting a different substance out of cell
• Symporters
• transport two different substances in the same direction

slides.title: Active Membrane Transport
slides.english_text:
Active Membrane Transport
• Vesicular Transport (Bulk Transport)
• Involves transport of many molecules, large molecules (E.g. large protein molecules), and fluids across membrane by forming vesicles
• Requires cellular energy
• Vesicular transport processes include:
• Endocytosis: transport into cell
• Exocytosis: transport out of cell

slides.english_text:
Active Membrane Transport
• Endocytosis
• Involves formation of vesicles by invagination of cell membrane to transport certain substance into cytoplasm
• Example: Phagocytosis
• The cell engulfs a large particle by enclosing it within a vesicle called a phagosome. The phagosome is then combined with a lysosome.

slides.title: Membrane Transport and Membrane Potential
slides.english_text:
Membrane Transport and Membrane Potential
• Selective permeability of cell membrane leads to different concentrations of charged particles in cytoplasm and in extracellular fluid. This results in membrane potential, the difference of voltage across the cell membrane.
• In resting state, resting membrane potentials of all human cells range from - 50mV to -100mV, depending on cell type.
• negative sign (-) indicates inside of cell is more negative than outside of cell
slides.raw_bilingual_text:
Membrane Transport and Membrane Potential
跨膜運輸與膜電位
• Selective permeability of cell membrane leads to different concentrations of
charged particles in cytoplasm and in extracellular fluid. This results in
membrane potential, the difference of voltage across the cell membrane.
細胞膜的選擇性通透性導致細胞質和細胞外液中帶電粒子濃度不同，這導致
膜電位，即細胞膜內外的電壓差。
• In resting state, resting membrane potentials of all human cells range from -
50mV to -100mV, depending on cell type.
在靜息狀態下，所有人體細胞的靜息膜電位範圍為 -50mV 至 -100mV，具體
取決於細胞類型。
• negative sign (-) indicates inside of cell is more negative than outside of cell
負號(-)表示細胞內部比細胞外部電壓更負

slides.title: Membrane Transport and Membrane Potential
slides.english_text:
Membrane Transport and Membrane Potential
• Generation and Maintaining of Resting Membrane Potential
• (1) Proteins with negative charge are too large and polar. They cannot pass across cell membrane and will be trapped inside cell.
• (2) Cell membrane is somehow more permeable to K +. K + are transported out of cells by facilitated diffusion.
• (3) Action of Na + /K + pump brings more ions with positive charge out of cell.
• Change of membrane potential is very important for the function of muscular system and nervous system.
slides.raw_bilingual_text:
Membrane Transport and Membrane Potential
跨膜運輸與膜電位
• Generation and Maintaining of Resting Membrane Potential
產生和維持靜息膜電位
• (1) Proteins with negative charge are too large and polar. They cannot pass across
cell membrane and will be trapped inside cell.
帶負電荷的蛋白質分子太大且極性太強，不能穿過細胞膜，會被困在細胞內。
• (2) Cell membrane is somehow more permeable to K + . K + are transported out of cells
by facilitated diffusion.
細胞膜某程度上對鉀離子的滲透性更強，鉀離子通過促進擴散從細胞中轉運出來。
• (3) Action of Na + /K + pump brings more ions with positive charge out of cell.
鈉鉀泵的活動將更多帶正電荷的離子帶出細胞。
• Change of membrane potential is very important for
the function of muscular system and nervous system.
膜電位的變化對肌肉系統和神經系統的功能非常重要。
